review.notes:
Upstream codes 511000824 and 511000825 are artwork variants of one implementation (identical cdb text, identical script diff, codes within +/-10), folded per instruction 4 with the lower code as historical_passcode. The third upstream entry, 511027037 'Ring of Destruction (Manga)' in the unofficial script folder, is a different card - it activates on EVENT_ATTACK_ANNOUNCE against the attacking monster and damages only the opponent - so it is not a period TCG implementation and is excluded rather than escalated. Pre-baseline lineage v0 -> v4 is cosmetic ('Direct Damage' -> 'damage', 'to the Life Points of both you and your opponent' -> 'to both players', 'Select and destroy' -> PSCT 'Target ... destroy that target, and if you do'); the pre-errata script keeps EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET, so the select/target rewording is not a targeting change. This card does not appear on EdisonFormat.com's Functional Errata page, so no community corroboration is cited; the erratum is dated solely from the lineage printing.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Ring of Destruction). The rulings read support d4, d5 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved (general rule only) at Edison, unresolved (general rule only) at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d3 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d4 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d5 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d6 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (PGL2-EN063, Premium Gold: Return of the Bling) Independently corroborated by Konami's own errata announcement and the archived Forbidden & Limited List page carrying its effective date; the printing remains the anchor because it is when the text first became available in the TCG (the announcement and the F/L effective date differ by a few days).

event.historical_text: Target 1 face-up monster on the field; destroy that target, and if you do, inflict damage to both players equal to that target's ATK.
event.modern_text: During your opponent's turn: Target 1 face-up monster your opponent controls whose ATK is less than or equal to their LP; destroy that face-up monster, and if you do, take damage equal to its original ATK, then inflict damage to your opponent, equal to the damage you took. You can only activate 1 "Ring of Destruction" per turn.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the errata'd card may only be activated during your opponent's turn, may only target a face-up monster your opponent controls whose ATK is at most that opponent's LP, deals YOU damage first equal to the destroyed monster's ORIGINAL ATK and only then an equal amount to your opponent (and none if you are already at 0), and is limited to one activation of 'Ring of Destruction' per turn. The pre-errata script matches the older printed text: no turn condition (s.condition and Duel.IsTurnPlayer(1-tp) absent), any face-up monster on either field as target, no LP ceiling, no SetCountLimit, and simultaneous damage to both players computed from the monster's current ATK (two deferred Duel.Damage calls closed by Duel.RDComplete()).

rulings_check.difference: Era: no turn condition; a Set Ring of Destruction can be activated during either player's turn. Modern (2015): only during your opponent's turn. Era: may target any face-up monster on the field, either player's. Modern: only a face-up monster your opponent controls. Era: no ceiling on the target's ATK. Modern: the target's ATK must be at most your opponent's Life Points. Era: the damage equals the destroyed monster's CURRENT ATK (counters, Equips, doublers apply). Modern: equal to its ORIGINAL ATK. Era: Ring deals the full damage to BOTH players at once. Modern: you take the damage first, then your opponent takes an equal amount (and nothing if you are already at 0 Life Points). Era: no limit on Rings per turn. Modern: 'You can only activate 1 "Ring of Destruction" per turn'.
